item.title: Account Director (Health | Life Sciences | Public Affairs)
item.description: PLMR Healthcomms a leading UK healthcare public affairs and communications consultancy. We help organisations get health innovation moving. Working across pharmaceuticals, medical technology, diagnostics, digital health and the wider NHS, we help clients navigate complex policy and NHS structures to turn innovation into real-world impact. As the NHS continues to evolve, organisations need advisers who understand how decisions are made across government, Parliament and the NHS. Our team combines expertise in health policy, public affairs, strategic communications and stakeholder engagement to help clients shape policy, build trust and accelerate adoption. As part of the wider PLMR Group, we bring together specialists in communications, digital, political intelligence and AI-enabled insight to deliver integrated campaigns that influence policy, change perceptions and create measurable impact. We judge our success by the difference we make for our clients - whether that's influencing policy, strengthening partnerships, changing conversations or helping innovative products and services reach patients more quickly. Key Responsibilities and Duties We're looking for an experienced and ambitious Account Director to help lead the next stage of PLMR Healthcomms' growth. This is an opportunity to work at the heart of some of the most important challenges facing healthcare today. You will be supporting organisations to navigate NHS reform, shape policy, build stakeholder confidence and ultimately improve patient access to medicines, technologies and services. You will act as a trusted adviser to clients across pharmaceuticals, medical technology, diagnostics and digital health, helping them move from ambition to action. Alongside leading strategic client programmes, you will play an important role in developing our growing healthcare practice, supporting new business, mentoring colleagues and helping strengthen PLMR Healthcomms' reputation as the consultancy that gets health innovation moving. The ideal candidate will bring: A passion for improving healthcare through policy, communications and stakeholder engagement. Significant experience advising pharmaceutical, life sciences or health technology organisations, ideally with agency experience. An excellent understanding of the NHS, Government, Parliament and the wider healthcare policy landscape. Confidence advising senior clients through complex policy, political and reputational challenges. A commercial mindset and enthusiasm for helping grow both clients and the wider business. A collaborative approach and a desire to develop colleagues while contributing to a supportive, ambitious team. Key Skills and Competencies Significant experience in healthcare public affairs, integrated communications or healthcare consultancy. A strong understanding of the political and NHS landscape and how healthcare decisions are made. Experience advising pharmaceutical, medtech or life sciences organisations. A track record of leading strategic client relationships and delivering measurable outcomes. Excellent commercial awareness and experience contributing to business growth. Outstanding communication, leadership and mentoring skills. Curiosity, ambition and a desire to help shape the future of healthcare. To Apply Please click the Apply button below to find out more about this role. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Saturday 31st October 2026

item.title: Public Affairs Consultant
item.description: We are looking to hire a Public Affairs Consultant to join our expanding team. NorthPoint works where politics, regulation, reputation and the media intersect. We help organisations navigate that environment, influence policy and public discourse, and protect their standing when the stakes matter. Our strength lies in understanding how decisions are made, how reputations are formed and how organisations can engage effectively with Government, regulators and the media. We provide senior counsel that helps clients anticipate change, manage risk and act decisively at the moments that matter most. We advise organisations across the public, private and third sectors, from ambitious start-ups and scale-ups to established national and global outfits. We work across a broad range of sectors, with particular expertise in industries where political, regulatory and public scrutiny shapes commercial success. This role encompasses both internal and external responsibilities, requiring an individual who excels in clear, direct communication. It is ideal for someone who: Is a proactive individual with experience in public affairs or government relations. Has strong understanding of Parliament, Government and how policy is shaped and influenced. Has a political and/or public affairs network and is comfortable at networking events. Is happy to get stuck in on new business growth. Can bring a sense of humour and enthusiasm to the table (work doesn't have to be dull). Has agency experience and looking for more autonomy Can cultivate strong relationships with stakeholders across all levels (personality is key, no shrinking violets). To Apply Please click on the Apply button below to email your CV and a short paragraph (no more than a few sentences) about why you'd be a good fit, and when applying clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. The successful candidate must have permission to work in the UK before the commencement of employment. Interviews will be on a rolling basis and we might appoint a candidate before the closing date. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Monday 26th October 2026

item.title: Policy Officer
item.description: Do you want to work at the heart of heritage, and help to champion its future? The Heritage Alliance is seeking a part-time Policy Officer to join our small advocacy team at an exciting time for the sector. The role will support with all elements of our research, policy development and political engagement. This role would be ideally suited to someone looking to gain experience in the heritage sector who has a keen interest in the UK policy and political landscape. The Heritage Alliance is the national umbrella body for heritage, a charity with over 200 organisational members. This is an exciting and wide-ranging role, requiring a dynamic, proactive and reliable individual. The role presents an ideal opportunity for someone looking to develop skills in policy research and development, political communications, and parliamentary monitoring. The role gives an opportunity to work with a small team to build expertise in a diverse range of policy areas including planning, historic landscapes, education and skills, and funding. Key priorities for 2027 include advocating for heritage through the government’s devolution and rewiring the state agenda, publishing and promoting reports on placemaking and academic partnerships, and strengthening our relationships with the new administration and regional decision-makers. Applicants should be persuasive writers and communicators, have a passion for advocacy and policy, strong analytical skills, and the ability to deliver at pace. Whilst a demonstrable interest in heritage is important, direct experience is not essential. Key Responsibilities: Researching across a wide range of policy briefs affecting the Alliance’s members; Drafting letters, briefings and consultation responses for government and parliament as needed; Co-ordinating, minuting and actioning the work of the Alliance’s Advocacy and Working Groups in liaison with their Chairs; Monitoring parliamentary activity for heritage-related developments in both houses and in select committees; Supporting with the development and drafting of policy and insight reports, advocacy resources and publications; Occasional support of the Heritage Alliance’s communications and events products, including producing copy and reporting on government news and policy developments for our newsletters. To Apply Please click the Apply button below to find out more about this role and to download the Application Form. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. The closing date for applications is 9 November with interviews held at our offices shortly afterwards. The starting date for the new role would ideally be December 2026 or early January 2027. This role is part-time (0.5 FTE) for an initial 1-year contract with potential to extend. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Monday 9th November 2026

item.title: Public Affairs Officer
item.description: Groundwork UK is looking for a Public Affairs Officer to help put its new three-year public affairs strategy into action. About Us Groundwork UK is the national body of the Groundwork federation, supporting, championing and representing the work of Groundwork Trusts across the country. This includes building national relationships with funders and policymakers, securing resources to support local delivery and acting as a managing agent for programmes and contracts delivered by Groundwork Trusts and other partners. Groundwork takes practical action to create a fair and green future in which people, places, and nature thrive. We support local communities and businesses to build capacity and resilience as this is vital if we are to tackle hardship, achieve a just transition to net-zero and help nature recover in a way that reduces inequality and leads to better work and healthier, happier lives. About the Role This is a hands-on role focused on strengthening Groundwork’s political visibility, building relationships with key stakeholders, and supporting the federation to make a clear and compelling case for place-based environmental and social action. Working with the Head of Policy & Communications, the postholder will map and engage national, regional and devolved political stakeholders; maintain intelligence on policy developments and opportunities; and help Groundwork Trusts prepare for and follow up political engagement. The role will also support the development of briefings, correspondence, stakeholder materials and core messages that explain Groundwork’s role and impact. About You We are looking for someone with a genuine enthusiasm for politics, strong written communication skills and the judgement to understand what matters, what will land and how relationships are built over time. You will be organised, self-motivated and comfortable working with senior colleagues and external stakeholders across government, combined authorities, civil society and the wider policy landscape. To Apply If you would like to find out more, please click the Apply button below. You will be directed to our website where you will be able to download the Job Description and Recruitment Pack, and to complete your application for this position. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Interview Details: Week commencing 16 November - Birmingham office. We value diversity and flexibility in our workforce as we think it gives us access to a wider range of skills. We therefore strive to be an equal opportunities employer. Where appropriate, we ask our workers to complete a Disclosure and Barring Service (Criminal Records Bureau) check. No agencies please. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Friday 30th October 2026

item.title: External Relations Manager (Corporate Comms)
item.description: The External Relations Manager is a key role in West Midlands Police’s mission of ‘Working in partnership, making communities safer’ and our strategic communications and engagement approach, focused on building trust, satisfaction, and confidence among communities, partners, and our workforce. Acting as a trusted expert within the Corporate Communications Department and strategic advisor to the Force Executive Team, the postholder leads on the development of accessible, inclusive communications and engagement activity that positively influences outcomes, aligned with force objectives, and deepens our ability to develop policy and strategy with partners and senior stakeholders. This position provides strategic leadership for external and stakeholder engagement across the force, with the aim of identifying, building and maintaining relations to support the force achieve its strategic priorities. The postholder will be part of our experienced News and External Relations Team, closely working with the Chief of Staff, to maintain positive relationships with strategic stakeholders, such as across local authorities, bluelight services, the Combined Authority, local and regional politicians and members of Government, faith leaders and community advocates. The role will therefore require that the individual cultivates and owns relationships with a range of partners and stakeholders, proactively maintaining positive engagement and seeking out events and visits as advocacy opportunities. Key Responsibilities Strategic Communications: Develop and execute multi-channel external communications and stakeholder engagement strategies. Evaluate external relations and communications performance; Political & Stakeholder Landscape: Deep understanding of local and regional governance, including the mechanics of local authorities, the Combined Authority, bluelight services, and central government. Manage complex stakeholder relationships and build and maintain these as well as influencing and negotiating with senior colleagues and external stakeholders; Partnership Working: Identify, build and maintain high-level relationships with diverse external groups, including faith leaders, community advocates, and senior politicians. Identify, plan and execute high-impact visits and public events as advocacy opportunities; Executive Advising: Act as a trusted advisor to Executive Teams, Chief Officers, or equivalent senior leadership figures; Project Management: Deliver projects to time, budget, brief and manage risk. About us West Midlands Police is the second-largest police force in England, serving more than 2.9 million people across Birmingham, Coventry, Wolverhampton, Dudley, Sandwell, Solihull and Walsall. Every day, our people work together to keep our communities safe, protect vulnerable people, prevent crime and bring offenders to justice. We answer more than 2,000 emergency calls every day and provide policing 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Whether responding to emergencies, supporting victims, investigating crime or working behind the scenes, every role plays a vital part in delivering an outstanding service to the public. We're proud of the progress we've made in reducing crime, improving emergency response times and increasing arrest rates. These achievements are only possible because of the dedication, professionalism and expertise of our officers, staff and volunteers. As we continue to transform the way we police, we're looking for talented people who are committed to making a real difference. To Apply Please click the Apply button below to find out more and to download the Role Profile including the Essential, Desirable and any educational requirements for the role. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Interviews: 16th November. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:55pm on Sunday 1st November 2026
